text:
I read every tracked file except `package.json`. I didn't build the site, so these come from reading the source only. Findings are ordered by severity.

## High

1. **Every canonical points at a staging host.**
   - `src/_includes/base.njk:8` hardcodes `https://staging.brightside-dental.example{{ page.url }}`.
   - `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `geo.config.json` all use `https://www.brightside-dental.example`.
   - Search engines and AI crawlers are told the canonical version of every page is on staging, which conflicts with the sitemap.
   - Fix: build the canonical from the production origin, ideally one `site.origin` data value that `geo.config.json` also uses.

2. **The Services page is `noindex` but listed in the sitemap.**
   - `src/services.njk:5` sets `noindex: true`, and `src/sitemap.xml:4` lists `/services/`.
   - This is probably a leftover from a draft. It hides your main commercial page from search and AI answers, and it sends a contradictory signal.
   - Fix: delete line 5. Keep `noindex` only on `thanks.njk`, which is correctly excluded from the sitemap.

3. **The structured data is invalid JSON.**
   - `src/contact.njk:10` has a trailing comma after the `telephone` value. Parsers will reject the whole block, so you currently have no schema at all.
   - Fix: remove the comma.
   - Also add the fields the Dentist type needs for local and AI answers: `url`, `address` (a `PostalAddress` for 12 Park Row, Leeds), `openingHoursSpecification`, `image`, `areaServed` and `sameAs`. Write the telephone in international format (`+44 113 496 0000`).
   - Better: move the schema into `base.njk` or the home page so it appears site-wide, not only on Contact.

## Medium

4. **The Team page has no description.**
   - `src/team.njk:4` has no `description`, so `base.njk:7` outputs an empty `content=""`.
   - Fix: add one to `team.njk`, and make `base.njk` omit the tag or fall back to a default when `description` is missing.

5. **The content is too thin and unsupported for AI citation.**
   - `src/services.njk:8-9` is a bare list with no description, duration or price for any treatment. The line "Our prices are simple and clear" has no prices.
   - `src/team.njk:6` ("decades of experience") names no dentists, qualifications or GDC registration numbers.
   - `src/index.njk:7` ("Trusted by thousands") makes a claim with no source.
   - Fix: give each service its own section or page, with what it involves, who it's for, and price ranges. List named clinicians with credentials. Back up or remove the "thousands" claim. Add an FAQ and put the opening hours in visible text.

6. **The hero image is probably broken, and it isn't optimised.**
   - `src/index.njk:8` references `/img/reception.jpg`. No `img/` directory is tracked, and `.eleventy.js:1` passes through only `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`.
   - Fix: add the image and a passthrough for `src/img`. Also add `width` and `height`, and consider `loading` and `srcset`.

## Low

7. **The page template is missing basic metadata.**
   - `base.njk:2` has no `lang` attribute: use `<html lang="en-GB">`.
   - There are no Open Graph or Twitter tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`).
   - There is no `<h1>`-independent site name or favicon.

8. **The sitemap is hand-maintained.**
   - `src/sitemap.xml` is a static passthrough (`.eleventy.js:1`), has no `<lastmod>`, and will drift as pages are added.
   - Fix: generate it from the Eleventy collections, using the same origin value as the canonical.

9. **`src/contact.njk:8` uses `data-nosnippet`** on the insurance line. Leave it only if you meant to hide it from snippets and AI summaries. It's a compliance caveat that arguably belongs in them.

10. **Crawler access is fine but implicit.**
    - `robots.txt:1-2` allows everything, which matches `geo.config.json`'s `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
    - If you want the policy to be explicit and enforceable, add named `User-agent` blocks for the AI search bots (e.g. `OAI-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`). An `/llms.txt` summarising the practice is optional.

I'd start with 1–3, since they're one-line fixes and the largest problems.
